title: Texas's 17th Congressional District election, 2026
description: The race for Texas's 17th Congressional District pits incumbent Republican Pete Sessions against Democratic nominee Casey Shepard in a general election on November 3, 2026. The district, which covers Central Texas including Waco, Temple, and parts of Williamson County, was redrawn under a new map signed into law in August 2025 that is expected to net Republicans additional seats statewide. Sessions, a former House Rules Committee chairman who previously represented a Dallas-based district before returning to Congress from the Waco-area seat in 2020, was unopposed in the Republican primary. Shepard, a Waco indigent defense attorney, won a competitive three-way Democratic primary and subsequent runoff against Milah Flores on May 26, 2026. The Cook Political Report rates the race as 'Solid R,' reflecting the district's strong Republican lean under the new map.
polling_note: No public opinion polling was found for this specific general election race as of June 2026.

candidates.name: Pete Sessions
candidates.summary: Pete Sessions is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Texas's 17th Congressional District, first elected to this seat in 2020 after previously serving Congress from 1997 to 2019 representing Dallas-area districts. He chaired the House Rules Committee from 2013 to 2019 and served as chair of the National Republican Congressional Committee from 2009 to 2012. A native of Waco, Sessions worked for Southwestern Bell for 16 years before entering politics.

candidates.name: Casey Shepard
candidates.summary: Casey Shepard is the Democratic nominee for U.S. House in Texas's 17th Congressional District. A seventh-generation Texan and Waco-based attorney, Shepard has focused his legal career on indigent criminal defense since 2011, representing clients without financial resources. He won the Democratic nomination through a competitive primary and runoff, and his campaign emphasizes food access, health care, affordable housing, and fighting executive overreach.

forecast.rationale: No public general-election polling exists for this race as of June 2026. The forecast relies on non-polling indicators: the district was redrawn under a 2025 map described as favorable to Republicans and expected to net the GOP additional seats statewide; incumbent Republican Pete Sessions has extensive congressional experience (including as Rules Committee chair and NRCC chair) and was unopposed in the Republican primary; the Democratic nominee Casey Shepard won a competitive three-way primary and runoff but faces a heavily Republican district; and Cook Political Report rates the race as 'Solid R.' Confidence is medium rather than high due to the absence of race-specific polls.
